description.narrative: The development objective of Justice Services Improvement Project for Romania is to improve the efficiency and accessibility of targeted justice institutions. This project has four components. 1) The first component, Improving Operations of Courts and Institutions under MOJ Authority, aims support activities that increase community awareness of justice services. 2) The second component, Enhancing National Trade Registry Office Performance, aims to transform the existing manually operated archiving system into an online electronic archive system (EAS) making all business information available to the public. Currently, information is available only to NTRO staff. 3) The third component, Improving Prosecution Service Performance, aims to finance an integrated security system, including security equipment, video surveillance and access cards, at the Prosecutors Office attached to the Supreme Court of Cassation (PCCIJ) where much of Romania's sensitive prosecution work is undertaken. 4) The fourth component, Project Management, aims to finance the operating costs of the Department for Implementation of Externally Funded Projects (DIEFP) at the MOJ which will act as the project implementation unit for the project.
To improve the efficiency and accessibility of targeted justice institutions.

DIEFP (recurrent)The Borrower, through MOJ, shall operate and maintain DIEFP until the completion of the Project, and ensure thatit functions at all times in a manner and with adequate staffing and budgetary resources, all acceptable to the Bank.
EMP (recurrent)The Borrower shall carry out Project works in accordance with the relevant EMPs.

Project Operations Manual (recurrent)The Borrower, through MOJ, shall adopt and carry out the Project in accordance with aProject Operations Manual acceptable to the Bank.

comment.narrative: To assess the general public perception towards selected reforms, a questionnaire focused on the public opinion with regards to the justice reforms and the level of access to relevant information, particularly by persons within vulnerable groups, was launched in 2019. Data gathered from the population in the six towns that were surveyed were extrapolated to the entire target population for each town (individuals aged 18 and above, who pertain to a vulnerable group: persons with disabilities, sexual minorities, members of single parent families, victims of crime, Roma, women). Subsequent surveys have been conducted annually. The sixth report from October 2025 shows that 66% of respondents report not knowing of information campaigns on reforms. 34% of respondents report being aware of public campaigns on justice.

title.narrative: Compliance of select court facilities with EU standards for accessibility

comment.narrative: This PDO indicator has been achieved, with all three courts completed under JSIP exceeding the 90% compliance target. Compliance with EU standards is measured using a detailed checklist based on Romania's updated court design standards, collected through site surveys. Per the results framework, data was gathered at baseline and after construction at Costesti, Horezu, and Carei First Instance Courts (FIC), none of which met standards initially. A 2024 survey confirmed 97% compliance with standards for new courthouses at Costesti and 97.5% at Horezu; in 2025, Carei FIC reached 97.2% compliance for rehabilitated buildings. JSIP also financed works for a new courthouse for Târgu Neamt FIC, but construction will not finish before JSIP closes. Completion was transferred to the Foundations project, and Târgu Neamt will thus not be included in the PDO indicator value. The PIU plans a final survey under Foundations at Târgu Neamt after works completion and building handover to the FIC.

title.narrative: Compliance of select court facilities with EU standards for accessibility

comment.narrative: This indicator remains on track to be achieved. Compliance with EU standard is measured by a survey of the civil works sites against a detailed checklist of the standards. The baseline was set at the start of the project, and the three sites completed under the Project (Costesti, Horezu, Carei) are re-assessed following works completion. At baseline, none of the FICs under the project met EU standards. The survey to gather updated values on this PDO indicator for two sites (Costesti and Horezu) was finalized, confirming compliance of 97% at both sites. Another survey to measure compliance at Carei FIC will be carried out before project closure. As completion of Targu Neamt will be moved to Foundations and removed from the JSIP POM, this will not be included as part of the PDO indicator value. Since the designs for Carei and Targu Neamt FICs were prepared in line with the relevant accessibility standards, it is expected that both buildings will be in compliance with the EU standards.

actual.value: In the two courts that have been completed – Costesti and Horezu – the compliance has been measured at 97%.

title.narrative: User perception of accessibility at select sites

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the perception of plaintiffs as to the level of accessibility of selected court facilities being rehabilitated under JSIP. The baseline/current values represent the perception at the time of the baseline survey (prior to the start of construction) with the end target to be recorded following the completion of construction and court hand-over. Surveys were done in Costesti, Horezu, and Carei FICs with an average of satisfaction for user perception of accessibility at 89% (91% for Costesti FIC, 93% for Horezu FIC and 84% for Carei FIC).

title.narrative: Percentage of courts equipped to deliver critical e-justice services (as defined by the MOJ) including the support for e-filing for litigants, lawyers and any other professionals

comment.narrative: This indicator remains on track to be achieved. The indicator seeks to capture the percentage of courts equipped to deliver critical e-justice services (defined by MOJ) including support for e-filing for litigants, lawyers and any other professionals, through redesigned, expanded and upgraded ICT network and hardware infrastructure for all courts. An increase in the percentage of courts supporting critical e-justice services is expected following JSIP ICT investments (such as LAN hardware and mobile connectivity equipment). Out of the identified 240 courts, 108 already have sufficient LAN connections, leaving 132 courts in need of LAN microworks. To meet the target of 60% (of the 240 courts), the project needs to finance a minimum of microworks for 36 courts. At present, microworks are already completed at 14 courts, resulting in an indicator value of 51%. Works are ongoing at 23 other courts. At least 22 of those will be doneby project closure, ensuring the indicator will be met.

title.narrative: Percentage of courts equipped to deliver critical e-justice services (as defined by the MOJ) including the support for e-filing for litigants, lawyers and any other professionals

comment.narrative: This PDO indicator has been achieved, with 60.4% of existing courts equipped to deliver e-justice services. The indicator measures the percentage of courts able to provide key e-justice functions (such as e-filing for litigants, lawyers, and other professionals) using upgraded ICT networks and hardware, as defined by the Ministry of Justice (MoJ). At JSIP's restructuring, 108 out of 240 courts already had sufficient LAN connections, leaving 132 courts needing upgrades. To reach the 60% target, microworks were required for at least 36 courts; the project financed upgrades for 37 courts. All microworks were completed by October 2025, surpassing the target.

title.narrative: Percentage of critical ICT equipment provided to Courts that are vendor supported (as a share of all critical equipment in courts)

comment.narrative: The MOJ reported a decrease compared to December 2024, moving from 74% to 56% in June 2025. This decrease is linked to the advanced age of the project, as much of the equipment purchased under the project is now older than 5 years. The PIU initially defined ”vendor supported” for PCs as ”5 years or newer” so this year the approximately 7000 PCs delivered under JSIP to the courts in 2019-2020 have become older than 5 years so they no longer qualify as ”vendor supported”.

title.narrative: Percentage of critical ICT equipment provided to Courts that are vendor supported (as a share of all critical equipment in courts)

comment.narrative: The indicator was previously met and peaked at 96.4% in 2020. However, the MOJ reported a decrease from 74% in December 2024 to 56% in June 2025. This decline is due to the aging of equipment purchased under JSIP, as nearly 7,000 PCs delivered to courts in 2019–2020 are now older than five years and no longer qualify as “vendor supported” under the PIU's definition. Additionally, the total number of devices increased over time, with older PCs not retired and about 3,800 laptops added in 2023–2024, further impacting the percentage of supported equipment.

title.narrative: Internal user satisfaction with selected electronic justice services

comment.narrative: Target for user satisfaction of clerks was met in the final survey. Targets for user satisfaction of judges and lawyers were met in previous surveys. This indicator seeks to measure internal user satisfaction of quality/efficiency of existing and digitized processes/and systems through a survey. ICT investments and targeted training are expected to increase ease of working, the modernization of equipment, reliability of systems, and ability to perform their work duties in a safe environment complying with health guidelines. The data was collected from internal court users (court staff) and lawyers, as follows: • Min. 200 - max. 500 questionnaires internal users - lawyers • 100 internal user questionnaires – (50 civil judges and 50 clerks) Data was collected from 14 courts, organized in five geographic groups: Horezu + Vâlcea Courts, Coste?ti + Arge? Courts + Pite?ti COA; Tg Neam? + Neam? Courts + Bacau COA; Carei + Satu Mare Courts + Oradea COA; Calafat + Dolj Courts + Craiova COA.

actual.value: Judge satisfaction: 78%Clerks satisfaction: 95%Lawyers' satisfaction: 73% Since the last survey, user satisfaction among clerks has improved slightly, meeting the 95% target. The values for user satisfaction among judges (78%) and lawyers (73%) are lower than those of previous surveys. The current decrease appears to be due to an increase in “prefer not to answer” responses from participants, compared to the previous survey. This does not necessarily indicate increased dissatisfaction with e-justice services; however, it does affect the overall value for user satisfaction as only those who reported satisfaction with the services are included in that value. Targets for user satisfaction amount judges (98%) and lawyers (79%) were met in previous surveys.
